entries.title: Isaiah 33:1
segments:
To thee; Assyria, as the representative of all persecuting powers. 
 
God uses wicked nations, like Assyria and Babylon, as "the rod of his anger," to chastise his people for their sins.  But when he has accomplished this work, he destroys them as easily as he had before raised them to power.

entries.title: Isaiah 33:2
segments:
Unto us--their arm; the prophet's prayer for his people in view of the coming trouble.  In the second clause he passes, as is common with the prophets, from the first to the third person. 
 
The repentance and supplication of God's people is the signal of his interposition in their behalf.

entries.title: Isaiah 33:3
segments:
The tumult; caused by God's appearance in behalf of his people. 
 
The only stability of a nation is the prevalence among its citizens and in its counsels of wisdom, knowledge, and the fear of the Lord.

entries.title: Isaiah 33:4
segments:
Your spoil shall be gathered; the spoil of the Assyrian host by the Jews. 
 
  Like the gathering of the caterpillar; as locusts gather and devour every thing. 
 
  Shall he run upon them; more literally, "shall one run upon it;" that is, upon the spoil of the Assyrians.

entries.title: Isaiah 33:6
segments: Thy times--his treasure; the reference is to the Jewish people. Compare note on

entries.title: Isaiah 33:7
segments: Shall cry without; the reference probably is to the event recorded in

entries.title: Isaiah 33:8
segments:
He; the Assyrian. 
 
  The covenant;
Despised the cities;

entries.title: Isaiah 33:9
segments: Lebanon is ashamed--shake off their fruits; a figurative description of the desolation caused by the Assyrian invasion.

entries.title: Isaiah 33:11
segments:
Ye; the Assyrians. 
 
  Your breath; your proud and impious spirit.

entries.title: Isaiah 33:12
segments:
The people; the nations assembled against God's people. 
 
  As the burnings of lime; consumed as by the intense fire of a brick-kiln.

entries.title: Isaiah 33:13
segments: What I have done; what I, Jehovah, have done in the destruction of my enemies.  The immediate reference is to the destruction of Sennacherib's host.  But this represents the vengeance that shall fall on all God's enemies to the end of time.

entries.title: Isaiah 33:14
segments:
Are afraid; the terrible judgment of God on their enemies fills them with awe. 
 
  Who among us shall dwell; or, can dwell; the words of the hypocrites and sinners.  If such be the power of God's wrath, who can endure its fierce flame for ever? 
 
The terrible judgments of God upon the wicked in this world, are such an earnest of the awful retributions of eternity as ought to fill all sinners with amazement and terror.

entries.title: Isaiah 33:15
segments: vv 15-16. The man who makes God his confidence, and obeys his law, is safe amid the most fearful convulsions and revolutions of nations.

entries.title: Isaiah 33:16
segments: He shall dwell on high; the same almighty power that has overthrown the enemies of God's people, and filled sinners in Zion with amazement, shall be to the righteous a munition of rocks.

entries.title: Isaiah 33:17
segments:
The king in his beauty; the King of Zion in his divine beauty and majesty. 
 
  They shall behold--far off; the probable meaning is, that the righteous no longer shut up and straitened, shall behold distant regions added to God's kingdom.

entries.title: Isaiah 33:18
segments:
Shall meditate terror.  Where is the scribe? shall call to mind the former days of terror, exultingly asking, Where is the scribe? etc. The receiver--weigher, margin--and counter of the towers, are those of the Assyrian army. 
 
vv 18-19. Every present deliverance which God vouchsafes to his people is a pledge of all needful future help; and as such it should be remembered with devout thanksgiving and gladness.

entries.title: Isaiah 33:19
segments:
Shalt not see; shalt no longer see. 
 
  A stammering tongue; a foreign language.

entries.title: Isaiah 33:20
segments:
Shall ever be removed; this promise has its complete fulfilment to the spiritual Jerusalem, the church of God, of which the earthly Jerusalem was the representative. 
 
vv 20-24. Whatever future trials await God's church, the final issue of them all shall be her establishment in perpetual holiness and tranquility.

entries.title: Isaiah 33:21
segments:
Will be unto us a place of broad rivers; which give fertility and strength. 
 
  Galley with oars--gallant ship; that is, galley or ship of the enemy.  It shall be a safe river.

entries.title: Isaiah 33:23
segments:
Thy tacklings are loosed; the enemy are addressed under the figure of a dismantled ship. 
 
  A great spoil; the spoil of the Assyrian host. 
 
  The lame; among God's people; so powerless are their once victorious enemies.

entries.title: Isaiah 33:24
segments:
Inhabitant; of the spiritual Zion. 
 
  Shall be forgiven their iniquity; this promise was fulfilled to the Jews of Hezekiah's day only in a very imperfect sense.  It manifestly looks to the final issue of all God's interpositions in behalf of his church, of which the overthrow of Sennacherib was an illustrious example.
